title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
source: canonical Two Sum II concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of integers numbers sorted in non-decreasing order, and an integer target. Return the positions of the two values whose sum is target as [i, j], counting positions from 1 and with i < j. Exactly one such pair exists in every input, and the two positions are different.
constraints: numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: Position 3 holds 4 and position 4 holds 5; no other pair sums to 9.

hints: The sort is a gift: when the current sum is too small, which direction can the smaller side still move?
Set one pointer at each end. If the sum is too small only moving the left pointer can raise it; if too large only the right pointer can lower it.
While left < right: compute total = numbers[left] + numbers[right]. If total == target return [left + 1, right + 1]; if total < target advance left; otherwise retreat right.
solution: Two pointers at both ends converge inward: a too-small sum moves the left pointer right, a too-large sum moves the right pointer left. The sorted order guarantees no valid pair is skipped, so the unique answer is found in one pass: O(n) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include negative values, zero, duplicate values, and pairs near the ends

visible.failNote: use the sorted order to skip impossible pairs
